failures.criterion: A reader joining after (here: during) an awareness flood is seen on the other process within a second, as on one pod (architect's scope; spec item 1)
failures.evidence: Red test TestAReaderJoiningDuringALiveAwarenessFloodIsSeenOnTheOtherProcess in packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/awareness_flood_multiprocess_test.go (commit 57348fc7). Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<url> go test -tags multiprocess -run TestAReaderJoiningDuringALiveAwarenessFloodIsSeenOnTheOtherProcess ./cmd/dispatch. Setup: one tab on A keeps 2,048 invented awareness clients alive by re-announcing them every 10 s. At 65dccc7c it fails 2 of 2: alice, joining A, 'was seen at once by carol on A but not by bob on B within 1s'. A probe found bob still had not seen her 76 s later while the tab kept re-announcing. At 1d55e48f, before the room bound, it passes 2 of 2. d7ceabb4 also fails this case (alice seen after 1 min 44 s, once a non-heartbeating flood expired). Cause: maxAwarenessClientsPerRoom (256) counts every client the room holds. A's room is full of the tab's clients, so it refuses alice's client id and never relays it, while A still sends her frame to its own peers. The next fix must pass all three red tests. One way: bound the client ids one socket may hold, rather than the room as a whole.
